reason: Ridge setback: roof plan and installer notes differ.
rationale: Five of the six applicable criteria are met with evidence in the packet. The ridge setback is unclear because the roof plan shows 18 in while the installer's field notes say the modules run to 14 in below the ridge to fit a third string. The reviewer must decide whether to require a corrected plan or accept the drawing and verify the setback at inspection.
letter:
Dear Denise Brooks,

Thank you for your application MIA-2026-1178 for a 7.0 kW rooftop solar array at 5120 Ibis Landing Court. Your documents meet the rooftop solar rules for the contractor licence, wind load, the electrical diagram, and equipment listings. One point needs to be cleared up before we can continue:

1. Ridge setback (Florida Building Code §RS-3). Your roof plan shows the modules 18 in below the ridge, but the installer notes say they run to 14 in below the ridge to fit a third string. The code requires at least 18 in so that firefighters can open the roof. Your contractor, Gulfstream Solar LLC, can send a corrected roof plan or confirm in writing that the array will be installed as drawn.

[Reviewer to decide: require a corrected roof plan at 18 in, or accept the plan as drawn and verify the setback at inspection.]

Please reply by 5 Oct 2026 through the applicant portal or by email to permits@example.com. Call (305) 555-0100 if you have questions.

Building Department, City of Miami
